subject: Geo-split pricing & reseller passback — EdgeHealth private offer
messages:
From: EdgeHealth Contracts <contracts@edgehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer geometry and reseller passback question

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at EdgeHealth is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we move to a private offer, procurement asked for a clean example of how you handle:

- Geo-split pricing (we want to bill US usage to EdgeHealth Inc. and EMEA usage to EdgeHealth EU)
- Reseller passback: our distribution partner (MediDistrib) expects a 12% passback on list before tax only for EMEA-origin usage
- Invoicing entity and tax treatment when a single private PO is used across marketplaces (AWS + Azure)

Can you provide a short waterfall example (list → discounts → passback → net to Redwood) and confirm whether the passback is applied to the invoice Redwood issues or a downstream settlement? Also include any implications for AWS Marketplace private offers vs Azure Private Offers.

Attached is our high-level commit expectation (annualized $1.2M, 65/35 split US/EMEA).

Thanks,
---
Maya Patel
Head of Procurement, EdgeHealth
contracts@edgehealth.com
[Attachment: EH_commit_Summary.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: EdgeHealth Contracts <contracts@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer geometry and reseller passback question

Hi Maya — great to hear and thanks for the commit doc. Looping in Ben (pricing lead) and Laura (finance ops) to give a concise example and confirm the operational approach. High-level answers while they draft a waterfall:

- Geo-split: we can support region-scoped metering so US usage invoices to EdgeHealth Inc. and EMEA to your EU entity; for marketplace private offers we typically map the payer by marketplace account/region.
- Passback mechanics: there are two common patterns we see:
  1) Redwood issues a single invoice to the buyer and then pays a separate settlement to the reseller (Redwood-managed passback).
  2) Passback is executed via the marketplace connect (AWS/Azure) where partner margins are reconciled by the marketplace/partner.
- Tax/invoicing: depends on your legal entities and the marketplaces. If you need separate invoicing per entity, we can split the offer by region/account.

Ben — can you draft a quick waterfall showing list price → Redwood discount → reseller passback (12% EMEA only) → final net? Laura — any FYI on tax/PO implications for a split-billing approach?

Next step: Ben will attach a spreadsheet; if it looks good we can produce a proposed PO term sheet and a DocuSign link.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer geometry and reseller passback question

Rachel / Laura — attaching a quick workback and sample waterfall. Key assumptions I used (please flag if any are off):

Assumptions:
- Committed annual list: $1,200,000 (65% US / 35% EMEA)
- Redwood proposed discount to EdgeHealth: 25% across both regions (negotiable)
- Reseller passback: 12% of list, applied only to EMEA-origin usage
- Marketplace fees: ignore for simplicity (we can layer later)

Waterfall (EMEA slice example):
- List (EMEA portion): $420,000
- Redwood discount (25%): -$105,000 → Customer net: $315,000
- Reseller passback (12% of list): -$50,400 → Net to Redwood: $264,600

US slice (no passback):
- List (US): $780,000
- Redwood discount (25%): -$195,000 → Customer net: $585,000
- Reseller passback: $0 → Net to Redwood: $585,000

Total net to Redwood (post passback): $849,600 on $1.2M list.

Operational notes:
- If EdgeHealth wants the passback to be visible on its invoice rather than a separate Redwood settlement, we recommend creating region-separated offers so the invoice lines reflect regional passbacks cleanly.
- AWS private offers can be structured to bill the buyer and then Redwood issues reseller settlements; Azure has similar mechanics but differs in invoice routing — Laura can confirm exact ledger treatment.

Attachment: channel_margin_workback.xlsx (contains the above broken into monthly phasing and quick sensitivity for 10–15% passback).

- Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Pricing | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: channel_margin_workback.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: Maya Patel <contracts@edgehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jun 2028 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer geometry and reseller passback question

Thanks Ben — the waterfall is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement/legal: 

1) We need the passback to be applied against the invoice lines that represent EMEA consumption so our distributor can reconcile monthly. If Redwood does a separate settlement to MediDistrib that’s fine, but the numbers must match invoice lines.
2) For tax purposes, EMEA usage must be invoiced by our EU entity (EdgeHealth EU BV). Can Redwood support a single private offer that splits billing per region to different legal entities, or do we need two offers?

AWS Marketplace has been looped in to confirm if their private offer can route invoices to two buyer entities — if not, we may need a split-off Azure/AWS approach and Redwood's side-by-side PO terms.

If we can see a proposed PO term sheet that shows regional billing lines and a clause committing Redwood to reconcile reseller passbacks monthly (with supporting CSV), we can move to signature.

Regards,
Maya
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <contracts@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer geometry and reseller passback question

Maya — thanks, and good clarifying questions. Quick answers and next steps below.

Short answers:
- We can support region-scoped billing to different EdgeHealth legal entities by creating two regional offer lines (one scoped to US payer, one to EMEA payer). That is operationally cleaner and makes monthly reconciliation simpler for your distributor.
- Passback approach: Redwood will provide a monthly CSV with usage by invoice line and a reconciliation file that matches the reseller settlement we issue to MediDistrib. The amounts will be derived from list pricing per the agreed waterfall (we'll include the formula in the PO terms).
- Marketplace differences: AWS tends to support private offers with buyer-account mapping; Azure can as well but the invoicing endpoints differ. We'll include both options in the term sheet and recommend separate region lines if EdgeHealth requires different invoicing entities.

Attachments & next steps:
- Attached: proposed_PO_terms.pdf (contains regional line items, passback formula, settlement cadence, and sample invoice extract).
- Legal: please share EdgeHealth legal/finance contact for the DocuSign. If you want, I can open a parallel Azure offer template while AWS confirms buyer-account routing.

If this is acceptable I'll generate a DocuSign (HubSpot deal EH-2028-043) and loop in Redwood Legal for a quick 48-hour review.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
Direct: +1 (415) 555-0123
